items.stem: What provides most of the energy that powers the water cycle?
items.explanation: Energy from the Sun heats liquid water and powers evaporation, which keeps the whole water cycle moving.

items.stem: Water leaves the ocean's surface and rises into the air. What state change is happening during evaporation?

options.text: Liquid water changes into water vapor
Solid ice changes straight into vapor

items.explanation: Evaporation is when the Sun's heat turns liquid water into water vapor, an invisible gas, that rises into the atmosphere.

items.stem: Plants release water vapor into the air from inside their cells. What is this process called?
items.explanation: Transpiration is the process of evaporation from inside plant cells into the atmosphere.

items.stem: Why do clouds form as water vapor rises high into the cold atmosphere?

options.text: The vapor is heated and expands
The vapor sinks straight into the soil
The vapor cools and condenses into tiny droplets

items.explanation: As vapor rises it cools and condenses back into liquid droplets. Billions of droplets together form a cloud.

items.stem: Rain, snow, sleet, and hail are all forms of what?
items.explanation: Precipitation is water that falls from clouds back to Earth when the droplets grow too heavy for gravity to hold up.

items.stem: After rain falls on a hillside, water flows downhill into streams and rivers. What is this moving surface water called?
items.explanation: Runoff is precipitation that flows across the land surface and collects in streams, rivers, and the ocean.

items.stem: Some rainwater soaks down into the soil and rock instead of flowing across the surface. What is this process called?
items.explanation: Infiltration happens when water soaks down into the soil and rocks below the surface.

items.stem: Water that soaks into the ground and collects in the spaces between soil and rock is called what?
items.explanation: Groundwater is water stored underground in pockets and spaces. Most of it eventually returns to the ocean.

items.stem: Besides the Sun's energy, what force pulls precipitation, runoff, and groundwater back downward?
items.explanation: Gravity pulls water downward, causing precipitation to fall and runoff and groundwater to move toward the ocean.

items.stem: Why do scientists say the water on Earth is never used up?

options.text: New water is constantly created by clouds
Water leaves Earth and is replaced from space
The same water is recycled endlessly through the water cycle
Plants make brand new water during transpiration

items.explanation: Water is not created or destroyed. The same water moves endlessly between the ocean, air, land, and living things in the water cycle.
